Method for assessing the influence of psychophysical state of 
drivers on control safety based on monitoring of vehicle movement 
parameters 
Samuil Gorelik, Vladimir Grudinin, Vladislav Lecshinskiy, Evgeny Khaskelberg * 
ITMO University, 49 Kronverksky Prosp., Saint Petersburg, 197101, Russia 
Abstract 
The authors solve the issue of identifying changes in the psychophysical factors of drivers’ health when driving without the use of 
special body sensors, which significantly expands the possibility of using the method f or drivers of any vehicles. The method 
allows us to determine correlations between the parameters of vehicle movement and the psychophysical state of the driver in the 
process of preliminary testing. For that purpose, a special mobile application is used making it possible to determine the subject’s 
reactions to dynamic images during a 1 –2-minute test and compare the results with the parameters of movement. The processing 
results represent correlation functions used to identify the signs of the driver’s sta te (fatigue, sickness, etc.), which affect traffic 
safety, by the parameters of movement. At the same time and in a similar way, factors related to the technical condition of t he 
vehicle are identified. For that purpose, correlation functions between the indicators of movement, obtained at the current moment 
and during previous trips, are calculated. The method can be used to improve the safety of transportation with the use of both public 
and individual vehicles (regarding drivers of private cars, mini electric vehicles, etc.). 
Keywords: monitoring; quality of driving; transportation safety.

2019, Skorokhodov et al. 2020, Soo et al. 2020, Vorozheikin et al. 2019). The interaction between the operator and 
the technical means determines the quality of basic functions’ implementation and safety for the surrounding objects 
and living environment. According to the modern view, a complex system consists of a set of objects with information 
interaction between them; co ntrol commands are executed following the results of the interaction and aimed at 
performing basic functions with the required quality and optimal resource consumption, and preventing incidents of 
various nature that affect physical and environmental safety. The automated control of the HMS is based on monitoring 
the parameters of the system objects in real time during the technological process. If the number of parameters being 
monitored becomes large enough (e.g. more than a few dozen), then the accuracy and reliability of monitoring data 
start to limit the ability to make proper control decisions and result in a high level of statistical errors of the first and  
second type (such as “missing the target” and "false alarm"), which are especially critical in the HMS since the safety 
of surrounding objects depends on them and the cost of an error is very high. 
2. Theoretical studies 
The task of optimizing the monitoring system in order to reduce the number of simultaneously estimated parameters 
so as to reduce statistical errors in monitoring and decision -making is crucial and required in many practical 
applications. This article considers an approach to solving the above issue based on a two-stage monitoring procedure 
using the analysis of changes in information e ntropy (first stage) and detailed estimates at the second stage if the 
growth of information entropy of the HMS reaches a statistically significant level (pre-crisis situation). HMS entropy 
is a characteristic of the dynamic stability of the system. Follow ing Gorelik et al. (2016a), we will consider entropy 
as an information characteristic of the HMS. It is obvious that changes in the HMS parameters vary the amount of 
information (entropy) that can describe it. The converse is also true: when the entropy in dicators change, the 
parameters of the system change as well. The rate of change of the parameters or entropy indicators characterizes the 
dynamics of changes in the HMS relative to the surrounding ecosystem. It is possible to perform an indirect assessment 
of the amount of information required to describe the controlled object by assessing changes in the output integral 
parameters of the HMS relative to their predicted values. In this case, the HMS is described by a phenomenological 
model of the “black box” type. The absolute difference between the actual and predicted (target, “normal”) values is
